issues.legal_issue: A dispute concerning the apportionment of compensation, or the persons to whom it is payable, under the National Highways Act must be referred by the competent authority to the Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction.
The District Magistrate, acting as an arbitrator under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, has no jurisdiction to decide a dispute concerning apportionment of compensation.
The competent authority’s summary power to determine shares under Section 3H(3) does not replace the statutory requirement to refer an apportionment dispute to the Principal Civil Court.
